sn12.20:1.2: Dependent origination is the process, the dependently originated phenomena are the product.
sn12.20:2.3: The principles of the Dhamma are not impermanent, since they are not existing things. Rather, they describe a process which is always observable, so it is always true to describe it in that way. See [an3.136](), where the same idea applies to impermanence, suffering and not-self. Also see Poṭṭhapāda at [dn9:31.10]().
sn12.20:3.17: This phrase is also at [sn12.1:2.14](). Note that there is no corresponding “dependent cessation”. The ending of dependent origination is Nibbana, extinguishment.
